newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Plains cattle market quiet, no sales-feedlots.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Plains cattle market quiet, no sales-feedlots.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle markets Friday were extremely quiet, with no sales of slaughter steers or heifers reported, feedlot sources said.
Most of this week's showlist were sold Wednesday in active trading that saw prices climb $1.00 per cwt, to $73.00, compared with last week.
Prices were supported by tight supplies of market-ready cattle and higher boxed beef prices this week, according to the feedlot sources.
The beef prices were underpinned by low stocks following two weeks of light slaughter.
However, this week's beef production expanded 2.5 percent from last week and eased supply concerns, but also spurred talk that beef prices would start falling as a result.
The prospect of weak beef prices in the face of strong fed cattle prices reportedly pushed large processors to consider cutting back on production next week, market sources said.
If beef production is reduced, the lighter packer demand could offset potential strength from tight supplies of finished cattle.
